title: Texas AG Sues Fake Childcare Firm Over H-1B Visa Scam
excerpt: Ken Paxton alleges Golden Qi Holdings, owned by Chinese national Yuan Yao, ran sham daycares to sell H-1B sponsorships for $20,000
body:
**Shell Daycares, Real Visas**

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has sued Golden Qi Holdings LLC and its owner, Chinese national Yuan Yao, for allegedly operating fake childcare centres across the Dallas area as fronts to fraudulently obtain H-1B work visas. The complaint, filed under the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act, alleges that the company submitted over 50 labour applications for roles such as software developers — positions entirely unrelated to childcare — while advertising non-existent daycare services.

Workers reportedly paid up to $20,000 each for sponsored visas, according to the state's filing. Paxton is seeking injunctions and civil penalties of up to $10,000 per violation.

**Part of a Wider Dragnet**

The lawsuit is the sharpest action yet in Paxton's broader investigation of 30 North Texas firms suspected of using "ghost offices" — rented addresses or virtual suites presented as legitimate worksites — to game the H-1B system. The probe, launched in January 2026, has demanded payroll records and contracts from dozens of companies.

**Diaspora Impact**

The case lands amid a febrile political climate around H-1B visas, with a new $100,000 federal fee on fresh petitions and rising tech-sector layoffs stoking anxiety among Indian-American workers who constitute the programme's largest beneficiary group. Each fraud case adds ammunition to restrictionist arguments — making legitimate visa holders collateral damage.

sources.label: Texas AG Office via EIN Presswire
